question: What are the ASOS (Automated Surface Observing System) network's precipitation observations, taken as one dataset: which products carry them (1-minute DSI 3285 pages 1 and 2, 5-minute DSI 6401, hourly and special METAR/SPECI as NCEI archives them (ISD/Global Hourly, now GHCNh), daily and monthly summaries CF6/F-6 and DSM), where is each stored and served (NCEI, AWS NODD noaa-global-hourly-pds and noaa-isd-pds, IEM, NWS and FAA real-time feeds), what goes into them (station counts by agency, precipitation sensors, station processor, data path to NCEI, human augmentation, measured vs derived values), and which organizations make them (NWS, FAA, DoD, NCEI, contractors, outside groups)? AWOS only to say how it differs. Each finding judged against RRS-1 "two or more geographically independent copies", D-2 "storage is a single point of failure", DIRS-3 "depends on external data feeds" and DIRS-4 "needs outside processing infrastructure". Out of scope: quality control, people, funding amounts, recent developments.
tier_reason: standard: several dimensions (products, hosts, inputs, organizations); not a set of 15+, no year series, no dispute in scope
